land.text: 'Australian mandate commencing 17 December 1920' over Kaiser-Wilhelmsland, the Bismarck Archipelago and the North Solomons: the part of Papua New Guinea outside Papua

successors.note: Held under Australian military occupation from September 1914; the Treaty of Versailles (28 June 1919) took Germany's colonies, the mandate began 17 December 1920 (infobox).

land.text: the Caroline Islands, Palau, the Mariana Islands (except Guam) and the Marshall Islands: 'The islands north of the equator became the Japanese League of Nations Mandate for the South Seas Islands'

successors.note: Japan occupied them from 1914 (infobox 'Japanese occupation: 29 September 1914').

land.text: Nauru: Australian troops 'held control until 1920', then the League of Nations mandate (History of Nauru)

successors.note: Nauru is not in the German New Guinea page's list of successors; the History of Nauru page gives the Australian capture in 1914 and control until 1920, and the mandate conferred in 1923.

capitals.name: Simpsonhafen (Rabaul)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Simpsonhafen (1910-1914)'; the page mentions Rabaul only as a battle location, so the modern name is the researcher's.

correction.text: 'the German flag was flown over Kaiser-Wilhelmsland, the Bismarck Archipelago' (3 November 1884); the mainland and the Bismarck Archipelago, here the part of Papua New Guinea outside the six Papuan provinces and outside the North Solomons

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 886 cells, about 224,000 km2 by the gazetteer; the page's table gives Kaiser-Wilhelmsland about 181,650 km2 and the Bismarck Archipelago about 49,700 km2 (231,350 km2 together, ratio 0.97). The page gives no Anglo-German boundary, so the Papuan provinces stand in for British New Guinea (the same split as the commonwealth-of-australia dossier). Cliopatria's German Empire row draws 810 cells (about 205,000 km2) of Papua New Guinea in 1890 to 1910 but no Micronesia.

correction.text: adds the North Solomon Islands (Bougainville, Buka): 'the North Solomon Islands were declared a German protectorate in 1885'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 922 cells, about 233,000 km2; the page's table has Bougainville 9,318 km2 and Buka 492 km2 on top of the 231,350 km2 of 1884, 241,160 km2 together (ratio 0.97).

correction.text: adds 'The Caroline Islands, Palau, and the Mariana Islands (except for Guam)', bought from Spain in 1899: 'These islands became a protectorate and were administered from German New Guinea'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Micronesian islands are a handful of cells (Caroline Islands about 2,150 km2, Palau 466 km2, Marianas 461 km2 on the page); the Marshall Islands (a German protectorate since 1885) join only in 1906.

correction.text: adds the Marshall Islands and Nauru: 'The Marshall Islands, which had been a German protectorate since 1885, were annexed to German New Guinea in 1906'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the colony at its fullest, 249,500 km2 on the page ('The total land area of German New Guinea was 249,500 square kilometres'); the gazetteer's cell count is about 235,000 km2 (ratio 0.94). Held to 1920 as the owner's shape: Australian occupation of the New Guinea part from September 1914 and Japanese occupation of Micronesia from the same autumn are occupation events, hatched over this shape.

region.text: Kaiser-Wilhelmsland and the Bismarck Archipelago, drawn as Papua New Guinea outside Papua and the North Solomons

ledger.note: 1884: the German flag is raised over northeast New Guinea and the Bismarck Archipelago (3 November 1884). 'On 3 November 1884, under the auspices of the Deutsche Neuguinea-Compagnie ... the German flag was flown over Kaiser-Wilhelmsland, the Bismarck Archipelago and the German Solomon Islands'; the Solomons are dated 1885 on the page. A chartered-company protectorate; Queensland's 1883 annexation had been repudiated by Lord Derby.

region.text: the North Solomon Islands: Bougainville (9,318 km2) and Buka (492 km2)

ledger.note: 1885: the North Solomon Islands (Bougainville and Buka) become a German protectorate: 'the North Solomon Islands were declared a German protectorate in 1885'.
1891: the seat moves from Finschhafen to Friedrich-Wilhelmshafen (infobox 1891-1899).
1899: the seat moves to Herbertshöhe (Kokopo), infobox 1899-1910.

region.text: the Caroline Islands, Palau and the Mariana Islands (except Guam)

ledger.note: 1899: Germany buys the Caroline Islands, Palau and the Marianas from Spain: 'The Caroline Islands, Palau, and the Mariana Islands (except for Guam) were bought from Spain in 1899.' 'These islands became a protectorate and were administered from German New Guinea.' A few grid cells.

1899: direct imperial control replaces the New Guinea Company: infobox 'Direct control established: 12 February 1899'. Same state, same colour (rule 2); the page does not describe the handover in its text.

1906: the Marshall Islands (and Nauru) are annexed to German New Guinea: 'The Marshall Islands, which had been a German protectorate since 1885, were annexed to German New Guinea in 1906'; the protectorate 'also included Nauru'. Two Marshall cells and one for Nauru.
1910: the seat moves to Simpsonhafen (Rabaul), infobox 1910-1914.

1914: Australia captures Nauru: after the outbreak of the First World War the island 'was captured by Australian troops' (History of Nauru; the Nauru page: 'captured and occupied by Australian troops'). The pages give no day.

region.text: Kaiser-Wilhelmsland, the Bismarck Archipelago and the North Solomons

ledger.note: 1914: Australia occupies German New Guinea. 'the Australian Naval and Military Expeditionary Force attacked the low-power wireless station at Bita Paka'; infobox 'Australian occupation: 17 September 1914'; 'On 21 September all German forces in the colony surrendered.' The commonwealth-of-australia dossier records the same occupation.

region.text: the Caroline, Mariana and Marshall Islands, held by Japan

ledger.note: 1914: Japan occupies German Micronesia: infobox 'Japanese occupation: 29 September 1914'; 'Japan occupied most of the remaining German possessions in the Pacific.' The empire-of-japan dossier records it with counterpart german-empire.
1920: the Australian military control of Nauru ends: Australian troops 'held control until 1920' (History of Nauru); the mandate itself is dated 1923 on the pages (terms drawn up in 1920).

1920: Nauru passes to the Australian mandate: 'The terms of the League of Nations mandate were drawn up in 1920' (Nauru), conferred on Australia in 1923 with the United Kingdom and New Zealand as co-trustees (History of Nauru). The territory-of-nauru dossier starts here.

region.text: Kaiser-Wilhelmsland, the Bismarck Archipelago and the North Solomons

ledger.note: 1920: the Australian military occupation of New Guinea ends as the mandate begins (17 December 1920).

region.text: the Caroline, Mariana and Marshall Islands, held by Japan

ledger.note: 1920: the Japanese occupation of Micronesia gives way to the League of Nations mandate for the South Seas Islands: 'The islands north of the equator became the Japanese League of Nations Mandate for the South Seas Islands.' The page does not date the mandate; December 1920 is the researcher's reading from the Australian mandate date.

region.text: Kaiser-Wilhelmsland, the Bismarck Archipelago and the North Solomons

ledger.note: 1920: New Guinea passes to Australia. 'After the Treaty of Versailles of 1919, Germany lost all its colonial possessions, including German New Guinea'; infobox 'Australian mandate: 17 December 1920'.

region.text: the Caroline, Mariana and Marshall Islands

ledger.note: 1920: German Micronesia passes to Japan as the South Seas Mandate: 'The islands north of the equator became the Japanese League of Nations Mandate for the South Seas Islands.'

region.text: German New Guinea as it stood in 1914

ledger.note: 1920: German New Guinea ends. The Treaty of Versailles (28 June 1919) stripped Germany of its colonies; the colony's land passes to the Australian mandate (17 December 1920) and the Japanese mandate. Nauru passes to territory-of-nauru (History of Nauru).

wars.name: Australian occupation of German New Guinea (First World War)

zones.text: Kaiser-Wilhelmsland, the Bismarck Archipelago and the North Solomons

wars.outcome: The Australian Naval and Military Expeditionary Force attacked Bita Paka; 'On 21 September all German forces in the colony surrendered'; the colony stayed under Australian occupation to the mandate of 17 December 1920.
wars.note: The page does not describe a Rabaul surrender on 17 September: that is the infobox's occupation date. The commonwealth-of-australia dossier cites other pages for Rabaul's capture on 12 September.

wars.name: Japanese occupation of German Micronesia (First World War)

zones.text: the Caroline, Mariana and Marshall Islands

wars.outcome: 'Japan occupied most of the remaining German possessions in the Pacific' (infobox 'Japanese occupation: 29 September 1914'); they became the South Seas Mandate.
wars.note: No fighting is described on the page.

certainty.note: The page gives no Anglo-German boundary on New Guinea (only the repudiated Queensland annexation 'east of the Dutch boundary at 141E'), so the land border with British New Guinea is approximate (drawn along Papuan province lines) and the interior highlands were barely administered. The island groups are fixed by their coasts.

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. One page opened for the colony (German New Guinea), asked twice, and one (History of Nauru) for Nauru alone. The brief's 2-5 pages were not used in full because the Anglo-German border and the Solomons line are not on this page; a gap-filler should open 'Kaiser-Wilhelmsland', 'Bismarck Archipelago', 'Anglo-German...' and 'German Solomon Islands'.
MODEL. The Territory is drawn with the same province split as commonwealth-of-australia: Papua = Central, Gulf, Milne Bay, National Capital District, Northern, Western; German New Guinea = Papua New Guinea minus those provinces (922 cells, Southern Highlands included although the Highlands were unadministered). The 1884 shape leaves out the North Solomons, which the page dates 1885 although its own sentence on 3 November 1884 lists the 'German Solomon Islands'.
COUNTERPARTS. Cliopatria's German Empire row (german-empire, 1871 to 1919) already draws 810 cells of Papua New Guinea in 1890 to 1910; the rendering should let this colony replace those cells. empire-of-japan's 1914 occupation_start and 1920 gain use counterpart german-empire; for the Micronesian islands german-new-guinea is the owner (Marshalls to 1906 are the German Empire's own protectorate, 1885 to 1906, which this dossier does not hold). The Japan dossier's gain is mirrored here as a loss to south-seas-mandate (colony dossier of Japan, written in this run). Nauru is held here from 1906 on the page's wording; the History of Nauru page (opened for Nauru only) gives the Australian capture in 1914 and control 'until 1920', and the territory-of-nauru dossier takes the island from 1920 (the Nauru and History pages disagree whether Nauru was joined to the Marshall Islands or to New Guinea in 1888, and on 1920 against 1923 for the mandate). The Spanish purchase has no month on the page.
NOT ON THE PAGE. The Anglo-German 1885 and 1886 agreements; the 1899 Samoa treaty; the date of the Australian capture of Rabaul (the Australian dossier gives 12 September 1914); the date of the Japanese mandate.
